mainTopic: When attached things count as one unit (חיבור): for שבת, for טומאה, and for הזאה.
overview: This amud is all about חיבור, the question of when two attached things count as one unit. It opens with a challenge to the ruling from the previous amud that opening a new shirt's neck on שבת is forbidden: why is that different from piercing a barrel's מגופה, which is allowed? רבא answers that the neck is part of the shirt, while the stopper is a separate object. Next, רבי ירמיה shows רבי זירא two משניות about חיבור לטומאה that seem to clash. רבי זירא explains that the deciding factor is whether the owner wants the items kept together when they are not in use. The גמרא then asks which תנא holds that anything attached to an object is like the object, and רב names רבי מאיר, based on the holders built into a stove. רבי מאיר's split ruling, טמא through contact but not through the air space, is explained as a deliberate rabbinic היכרא, so that people will not burn תרומה and קדשים by mistake. Finally, a ברייתא says separable tools are a חיבור for טומאה but not for הזאה. רבא begins to explain this: by Torah law, whether the tool is in use decides both laws the same way. The explanation of the ברייתא's split continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is opening a shirt's neck different from piercing a barrel stopper?
steps.stepSummary: A challenger compares the ruling from the previous amud, that opening a shirt's neck is forbidden, to the permitted act of piercing a barrel's מגופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this (opening the neck of a shirt) and the stopper of a barrel?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the ruling just stated on the previous amud, that opening the neck opening of a new shirt on שבת is a serious violation. Piercing a barrel's stopper is allowed, so why is this different? In the next step רבא defends the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a person makes a new opening in something on שבת. Piercing a barrel's מגופה is permitted, and the challenger argues it looks just like opening a shirt's neck. If the two cases are the same, רבא's strict ruling seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between
The clay stopper that seals a wine barrel
This one (here, the shirt's neck opening)

phrases.english: What is the difference between this and the stopper of a barrel?
phrases.notes: 'This' refers to opening the neck of a garment, discussed in the lines on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling about opening a shirt's neck from the preceding part of the daf; רבא defends it in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling from the previous amud that opening a shirt's neck opening on שבת is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Piercing a barrel's stopper also creates an opening, yet it is permitted. If the cases are alike, the shirt should be permitted too.

steps.title: The shirt's neck is part of the shirt, but the stopper is separate
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the neck opening is a built-in part of the garment, while the stopper is not part of the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: This one is connected, and that one is not connected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The shirt's neck is woven into the shirt itself, but the barrel's stopper is a separate piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you open the shirt's neck, you are finishing the garment and making it usable. That counts as completing a כלי. The stopper is only stuck onto the barrel, so piercing it does not finish or create any כלי. The idea of חיבור, whether something counts as one unit, decides the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Connected; counted as one unit with the main object
Not connected; a separate object

steps.whyThisMatters: The concept of חיבור introduced here is the link to the next exchange, which asks when attached items count as connected for טומאה.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
This is a connection, and that is not a connection.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the shirt's neck, which is part of the fabric; 'that' is the barrel stopper, a separate item.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: זֶה חִיבּוּר, וְזֶה אֵינוֹ חִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Opening a shirt's neck and piercing a barrel stopper are the same kind of act.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shirt's neck is part of the garment, so opening it completes a כלי. The stopper is separate, so piercing it makes nothing new.

steps.title: First source: temporarily joined items stay connected even when not in use
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a משנה showing that loosely joined items count as חיבור לטומאה until someone starts taking them apart, and infers that this holds even when they are not in use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה raised a contradiction to רבי זירא. We learned in a משנה: Launderers' basting stitches, a chain of keys, and a garment sewn with כלאים thread are considered connected for טומאה until one begins to untie them. So even when not in use, they are still connected.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up a contradiction. רבי ירמיה quotes the first of two משניות and draws a rule from it. The clashing משנה comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three items in this משנה are only joined temporarily. Each will eventually be separated. Even so, the משנה says they count as one unit for טומאה until someone actually starts separating them. רבי ירמיה concludes that they are connected even after the work is done, when they are just sitting there.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him (pointed out two sources that clash)
Loose temporary stitches a launderer uses to keep garments together
Forbidden mixture of wool and linen
Counted as connected, so טומאה touching one part reaches all parts
Apparently / this shows that
When not being used for work

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic, not a continuation of the שבת question. The only link to the previous lines is the word חיבור. Here it means connection for טומאה, not making a כלי on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised a contradiction before Rabbi Zeira:
We learned in a Mishnah: the basting stitches of launderers,
phrases.notes: Launderers loosely stitch customers' clothes together so they don't get lost.

phrases.english: and a chain of keys,
and a garment that is sewn with diverse kinds (forbidden thread)
phrases.notes: For example, a wool garment stitched with linen thread, which must be removed.

phrases.english: are a connection with regard to ritual impurity
until one begins to untie them.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה נָמֵי חִיבּוּר.
phrases.english: Apparently, even when not in use, it is also a connection.
phrases.notes: Keep this conclusion in mind, because the next source seems to say the opposite.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion linked to step 2 only by the concept of חיבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Temporarily joined items count as חיבור לטומאה even when not in use, until someone begins to separate them.

steps.title: Second source: an axe handle is connected only while in use
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה says a stick made into an axe handle is connected for טומאה only during use, which implies it is not connected when not in use.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted it: A stick made into an axe handle is connected for טומאה while in use. While in use, yes; when not in use, no!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the other half of the contradiction. This משנה suggests that attached items are not connected when they are not being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifies 'בשעת מלאכה,' while in use, and the גמרא reads this precisely. Only during use is the stick connected to the axe, so when it is not in use it is not connected. That directly opposes the inference from the first משנה, which said things stay connected even when not in use.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (here is a clashing source)
Axe
While in use, during work
Yes / no (used in a precise reading of the source)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: a stick that one made into a handle for an axe
is a connection with regard to ritual impurity while in use.
While in use, yes;
when not in use, no!
phrases.notes: The גמרא figures this out from how the משנה is worded; the משנה doesn't say it outright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the clashing source against the inference of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the first משנה that items remain חיבור even when not in use.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The axe-handle משנה limits חיבור to the time of use, implying no connection otherwise. That contradicts the first משנה.

steps.title: It depends on whether the owner wants them kept together
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the axe handle is tossed aside when not in use, but the laundered items are kept together on purpose even when not in use.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, when not in use, a person tends to throw the stick into the woodpile. Here, even when not in use, he wants them joined, because if they get dirty he will wash them again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא resolves the contradiction by showing that the cases are different. What matters is whether the owner wants the items to stay attached when they are not being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the axe, once the work is done the owner doesn't care about the stick and might toss it onto the woodpile, so it is not connected then. With the stitched garments, the owner wants them kept together even after the work, since it is easier to rewash them as one bundle if they get dirty. So whether something counts as חיבור depends on the owner's wish to keep it attached.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here (used to contrast two cases)
Likely to throw it away
It is pleasing to him; he prefers it
They get dirty
Whitens, launders

steps.whatToRemember: חיבור לטומאה depends on whether the owner wants the items kept together. If he still wants them joined when not in use (the laundered garments), they stay connected. If he discards one part after use (the axe stick), they are connected only while in use.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for many cases of attached items: the owner's attitude toward keeping them together determines whether they count as one unit.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: He said to him: There, when not in use,
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is answering רבי ירמיה. 'There' means the axe handle.

phrases.english: a person is likely to throw it among the wood,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה נָמֵי נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: here, even when not in use, he is pleased (to have them attached),
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the launderer's stitched garments and the other items in the first משנה.

phrases.english: for if they get dirty, he launders them again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) by the owner's intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות disagree about whether attached items are connected when not in use.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no disagreement. Items stay connected when not in use only if the owner wants them kept together. The axe stick is discarded, but the stitched garments are kept for rewashing.

steps.title: Who taught that whatever is attached counts like the object itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records that different yeshivos attributed this discussion to different אמוראים. It then asks which תנא is the source of the rule כל המחובר לו הרי הוא כמוהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught this teaching in the name of רב חסדא. In פומבדיתא they taught it in the name of רב כהנא, and some say in the name of רבא. Which תנא taught the rule the חכמים said: anything attached to an object is just like it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by asking which תנא is the source of the rule that an attached item shares the status of the main object. This question sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with when items count as joined for טומאה. Now the גמרא wants to find the earliest authority behind the general rule that something attached is treated like the main object. The opening lines only tell us who reported this discussion. They are not part of the argument itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught it (they reported this teaching)
A teaching or discussion
Which תנא taught this? (a request for the source)

keyTerms.term: כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לוֹ הֲרֵי הוּא כָּמוֹהוּ
keyTerms.meaning: Anything attached to it is just like it

steps.confusionAlert: סורא, פומבדיתא, רב חסדא, רב כהנא and רבא are not arguing here. These lines only record which name each yeshiva attached to this discussion. The actual question starts at מאן תנא.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught this teaching
in the name of Rav Ḥisda;
in Pumbedita they taught it in the name of Rav Kahana,
and some say it in the name of Rava:
Who is the tanna that taught this matter
that the Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לוֹ הֲרֵי הוּא כָּמוֹהוּ?
phrases.english: Anything attached to it is just like it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific cases of joined items to a search for the תנא behind the general rule of attachment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that something attached to an object has the same טומאה status as the object?

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר, based on the stove compartments
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב that the rule follows רבי מאיר. He brings a משנה where רבי מאיר says compartments built into a stove become טמא through contact but not through the air space, while רבי שמעון says they stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי מאיר. As we learned in a משנה: the holder for the oil jug, the holder for the spices, and the holder for the lamp that are built into a stove become טמא through contact, but they do not become טמא through the air space. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says they are טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the rule of attachment comes from רבי מאיר. He proves it from a משנה about small holders built into a stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שרץ touches the stove and makes it טמא, רבי מאיר says the attached holders become טמא along with it. That shows he treats attached items like the main object. If the שרץ is only inside the stove's air space, the stove becomes טמא, but רבי מאיר says the holders do not. רבי שמעון says the holders are not part of the stove at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The holder for the oil jug
The holder for spices
A stove
They become טמא through contact
Through the air space (the inside of a clay vessel)
Rules that it is טהור

steps.confusionAlert: Contact here means the טומאה touched the stove. It does not mean it touched the holders. The air space case means the שרץ was inside the stove without touching it. A clay vessel like this stove becomes טמא that way, but the holders do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה becomes the test case for the rest of the סוגיא. The גמרא will try to explain why רבי מאיר takes a middle position.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Meir.
As we learned in a mishna:
The holder for the cruse and the holder for the spices
and the holder for the lamp that are in the stove
become impure through contact
but do not become impure through the air space,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And Rabbi Shimon rules them pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא. דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by naming רבי מאיר and citing a supporting משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule follows רבי מאיר, who says attached stove holders become טמא when the stove becomes טמא through contact.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's middle position seems inconsistent
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's view makes sense, because the holders are not like the stove. But רבי מאיר's split ruling looks illogical. The holders should either be fully like the stove or not like it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון's view is understandable: he holds the holders are not like the stove. But according to רבי מאיר: if they are like the stove, they should become טמא even through the air space. If they are not like the stove, they should not become טמא even through contact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's ruling. It argues that he cannot hold both halves at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sets up an either-or. If the holders count as part of the stove, every way the stove becomes טמא should also apply to them. If they do not count as part of the stove, no way should apply. Becoming טמא through contact but not through air seems to fit neither option.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (this side makes sense, but...)
They are like the stove (count as part of it)
They should become טמא

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Shimon —
he holds they are not like the stove.
But according to Rabbi Meir,
if they are like the stove —
they should also become impure even through the air space.
If they are not like the stove —
they should not become impure even through contact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the internal logic of the רבי מאיר view cited in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's split ruling (טמא through contact, not through air)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: the holders either have the stove's status or they do not, so a partial result seems impossible.

steps.title: By Torah law they are separate; the חכמים added a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: Really, the holders are not like the stove. The חכמים made a גזירה that they become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, they are not like the stove. It is the חכמים who made a גזירה about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that by Torah law רבי מאיר agrees the holders are separate from the stove. Their טומאה through contact comes only from a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the dilemma. The holders do not share the stove's status by Torah law, so there is no automatic reason for them to follow the stove in every way. Their טומאה through contact is a rabbinic addition, and the חכמים can set its limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (introduces the true explanation)
They decreed (a rabbinic גזירה)

phrases.english: Actually, they are not like the stove,
and it is the Sages who decreed about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 8 by choosing the 'not like the stove' side and adding a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר must hold the holders are either fully part of the stove or fully separate.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law they are separate. Their טומאה through contact is only a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: Then the decree should cover the air space case too
steps.stepSummary: If the חכמים made a גזירה, it should also apply when the טומאה is only in the stove's air space.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they made a גזירה about them, then they should become טמא even through the air space!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It asks why the גזירה would stop at contact and not also include the air space case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים decided to treat the holders like the stove, the גזירה should seem to apply to every way the stove becomes טמא. The limit to contact only is still unexplained. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: If they decreed about them

phrases.english: If they decreed about them,
they should also become impure even through the air space!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גְּזַרוּ בְּהוּ, אֲפִילּוּ בָּאֲוִיר נָמֵי לִיטַּמּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 by asking why the גזירה is limited.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the holders' טומאה is a rabbinic גזירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה treating the holders like the stove should cover all forms of the stove's טומאה, including the air space.

steps.title: The split ruling is a deliberate signal so people won't burn תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים purposely limited their גזירה to contact only. This marks the טומאה as rabbinic, so no one will come to burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים made a distinguishing sign with them, so that a person will not come to burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. The חכמים left out the air-space case on purpose, as a sign that this טומאה is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, תרומה that becomes טמא must be burned. תרומה that is טמא only because of a rabbinic rule may not be destroyed. If the גזירה worked exactly like real Torah טומאה, people might burn תרומה that is really still טהור. The 'gap' in the גזירה shows everyone that this is a rabbinic level of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A distinguishing sign or marker that makes people aware of a difference
To burn
The portion of produce given to a כהן; it must be burned if it becomes טמא by Torah law
Consecrated (holy) items, such as sacrificial meat

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's 'half' ruling is not illogical. It is a deliberate rabbinic marker. The holders really are not like the stove, and the partial גזירה protects תרומה and קדשים from being burned by mistake.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים forgot about the air-space case, or that they were being inconsistent. The gap is intentional. It is the whole point of the answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea in ש"ס: the חכמים sometimes make a גזירה weaker than the Torah law on purpose, so that people will not treat the rabbinic rule as if it were Torah law.

phrases.english: The Rabbis made a distinguishing sign with them
so that a person will not come
to burn תרומה and consecrated items because of it.
phrases.notes: Burning these is forbidden unless they are טמא by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10's challenge: why the גזירה does not also apply when the טומאה is only in the stove's air space.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the limit of the גזירה as an intentional marker (היכרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the חכמים made a גזירה, it should cover every case where the stove becomes טמא, including the air space.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים purposely limited the גזירה to contact, so that the טומאה is clearly rabbinic and no one burns תרומה or קדשים because of it.

steps.title: Separable tools count as connected for טומאה but not for הזאה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that scissors made of separable parts, and the blade of a carpenter's plane, are a חיבור for טומאה but not a חיבור for הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: Scissors made of separable parts, and the blade of a carpenter's plane, are a connection for טומאה, but they are not a connection for הזאה (sprinkling).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with another 'split' ruling about whether parts are connected. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one part of these tools becomes טמא, the other part becomes טמא too, as if they were one unit. But when purifying them with הזאה (sprinkling the water of the פרה אדומה), sprinkling one part does not purify the other part. Each part needs its own sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: Scissors made of parts that are designed to come apart
The blade of a carpenter's plane, which can be removed from its handle
A connection; the parts are treated as one single item
Sprinkling the water of the פרה אדומה to purify from טומאת מת

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
scissors made of separable parts
and the blade of a carpenter's plane
are a connection for טומאה,
but are not a connection for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא that has a similar 'half-connected' ruling. It parallels the stove-holder discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separable scissors and a plane blade are a חיבור for טומאה, but not for הזאה.

steps.title: Either it is connected or it is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: if the parts are a חיבור, they should be one unit for הזאה too. If they are not a חיבור, they should not be one unit for טומאה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it there is a problem: if it is a connection, then it should be one even for sprinkling. If it is not a connection, then it should not be one even for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's split ruling as inconsistent. It uses the same kind of logic as the challenge in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether two parts are 'one item' seems like a simple fact about the object. A fact should not change depending on which law we are applying. So the ברייתא's half-and-half answer seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you want it.' This introduces a dilemma where both choices lead to a problem.
Also, too

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if it is a connection
then it should be one even for sprinkling too;
if it is not a connection
then it should not be one even for טומאה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling: a חיבור for טומאה but not for הזאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being connected is one fact about the object. It cannot be true for one law and false for another, so the split ruling looks self-contradictory.

steps.title: Torah law depends on whether the tool is in use
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that by Torah law the deciding factor is use. While the tool is being used, it is a חיבור for both טומאה and הזאה. When it is not being used, it is a חיבור for neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: By Torah law, while it is being used it is a connection, both for טומאה and for sprinkling. When it is not being used, it is not a connection, neither for טומאה nor for sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins answering the מה נפשך challenge by stating the basic Torah rule. He is setting up the explanation of where the ברייתא's split ruling comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that by Torah law there is no split: טומאה and הזאה follow the same rule. What changes the law is not which law we are discussing, but whether the tool is in use at that moment. Since this Torah rule has no split, the ברייתא's split must come from a rabbinic addition. That point is developed right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)
While the tool is being used for its work
When the tool is not being used

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's statement here does not yet explain the ברייתא's split. At the Torah level, there is no split at all. The difference between טומאה and הזאה will come from a rabbinic גזירה, just like the stove-holders case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This mirrors Steps 9–11. The Torah law is consistent, and the 'illogical' split ruling comes from a deliberate rabbinic layer on top of it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
By Torah law, while it is being used, it is a connection
both for טומאה and for sprinkling.
And when it is not being used
it is not a connection
neither for טומאה nor for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה חִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering Step 13's מה נפשך challenge by stating the Torah-level baseline.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates Torah law from rabbinic law; the deciding factor is whether the tool is in use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whether parts are connected is a single fact, so the ברייתא's split ruling is contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law, use decides, and טומאה and הזאה are treated the same. The ברייתא's split must therefore come from a rabbinic addition, which the גמרא explains next.
